The existing same-page thm-qa-shor-residue-sampler-correct-and-cost proves P(output a)=2^{-h}/(M/2^h)=1/M, nontermination probability lim_j(1-M/2^h)^j=0, and expected block count 2^h/M<=2. The algorithm specifies its input, fair-bit law, exact rejection loop and output; no additional prerequisite or item edit is needed.

Confirmed nonfatal notation/type defect: the Given declared x to be a residue class but then applied the integer class constructor [x^(q/2)]_N to it. Repaired only Given and proof step 2.1 by taking integer x with unit class [x]_N and applying order characterisation to that class. Squaring gives [x^q]_N=[1]_N; the true-order case excludes an identity half-power since 0<q/2<q. The original Statement is byte-identical; q=2 and N=2 boundaries remain sound.

Confirmed fatal dependency-citation defect: F7 dropped the cited definition's finite-space hypothesis and step 3.1 invoked it on infinite tape events. Repaired by constructing each attempt's finite terminal space (residue a, finite measurement transcript y) with normalized weights mu_a(y)/(N-1), restricting F7 to finite spaces, and applying finite coordinate independence to T terminal records. Unit conditioning now occurs only in the finite space; its good-unit mass >=1/2 and pointwise exact-order bound >=3/4 imply per-attempt success >=3/8, including immediate nonunit success. A finite union of null sampler nontermination events has zero mass. The Statement and CC/DC assumptions are unchanged.
